label: Bayes on Manifolds: Conditional Problems
notes: This chapter, printed pages 182 to 208, lifts the unconditional mixture machinery to conditional inference. When a predictor or response lives on a manifold, we model the joint or conditional density nonparametrically and read off regression curves and classifiers, all with Dirichlet-process priors and provable posterior consistency on curved sample spaces.

label: From Density to Regression
notes: The key move is that a flexible model for the joint density of predictor and response automatically yields a conditional density by division. Estimating one nonparametric object simultaneously delivers regression, classification, and testing, so the chapter only needs one prior on densities to drive every downstream conditional task on the manifold.

label: Product Kernels on Mixed Spaces
notes: Because predictor and response may live on different manifolds, the mixing kernel factors as a product of one kernel per coordinate. Each factor is a proper density on its own space, so the product remains a valid density on the product manifold while letting bandwidths and concentrations adapt independently across the mixed sample space.

label: Dirichlet Process Mixture Prior
notes: A Dirichlet process supplies the random mixing distribution, giving an almost surely discrete measure whose atoms become cluster locations. Its stick-breaking weights decay geometrically, the concentration parameter controls how many effective clusters appear, and the base measure seeds kernel parameters, producing an infinite, data-adaptive mixture on the product manifold.

label: The Nonparametric Regression Function
notes: Posterior draws of the joint density induce posterior draws of the conditional mean, the regression function of response given predictor. We summarize these by the posterior mean curve and surround it with pointwise credible bands, so uncertainty about the regression surface is reported honestly across every value of the manifold-valued predictor.

label: The Bayes Classifier
notes: When the response is a discrete label, the conditional density collapses to posterior class probabilities at each predictor location. The Bayes rule predicts the group maximizing that probability, minimizing misclassification risk. On shape spaces this means assigning a configuration to the group whose mixture explains its landmark coordinates most plausibly.

label: Decision Boundary on the Manifold
notes: The classifier partitions the predictor manifold into regions where one label dominates. The boundary is the locus where two posterior class probabilities tie, a curved surface that bends with the geometry rather than a flat hyperplane. Mixture flexibility lets this boundary capture clusters that linear discriminants would badly miss.

label: Posterior Consistency of Regression
notes: Under weak and strong neighborhood support of the prior and a compact manifold, the posterior for the joint density concentrates on the truth as the sample grows. Continuity of the conditional-mean functional then transfers this to consistency of the regression function, so estimates converge uniformly to the true response surface.

label: Consistency of the Classifier Risk
notes: Density consistency implies that estimated posterior class probabilities converge to the true ones, hence the empirical Bayes rule's misclassification risk converges to the optimal Bayes risk. The classifier is asymptotically optimal: with enough labeled shapes, no competing rule on the manifold can do systematically better.

label: Two-Sample Testing of Distributions
notes: To ask whether two groups share a distribution on the manifold, we place a nonparametric prior on each group's density and on a shared pooled density. Comparing the marginal likelihoods, or equivalently the posterior on a discrepancy between mixtures, yields a Bayes factor that weighs equality against difference without distributional assumptions.

label: Bayes Factor and Calibration
notes: The Bayes factor contrasts a model with one common density against a model with two separate densities. Large values favor a real group difference. Posterior predictive checks and simulation calibrate the factor's behavior under the null, guarding against overconfident rejections when sample sizes are small or kernels are misspecified.

label: Application: Shape Classification
notes: On landmark shape data the workflow distinguishes clinical groups by skull or bone configuration and classifies gender from shape. Predictors are points in Kendall shape space, kernels respect the quotient by rotation and scale, and the Bayes rule turns geometric clustering into a calibrated diagnostic prediction with reported uncertainty.

label: Synthesis and Workflow
notes: One nonparametric density model on the product manifold yields regression curves with credible bands, an asymptotically optimal classifier, and a calibrated two-sample test. Geometry enters through product kernels and invariant sample spaces; the Dirichlet process supplies flexibility; consistency theorems certify that the geometry-aware predictions are trustworthy as data accumulate.
